newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RALLYING-ERIKSSON EXTENDS LEAD IN NZ RALLY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-ERIKSSON EXTENDS LEAD IN NZ RALLY.

text.p: Kenneth Eriksson's hopes of securing his first win in the New Zealand rally were boosted on Tuesday when nearest rival Carlos Sainz of Spain hit a sheep during the opening stage of the third and final leg.
The Spaniard, a double world champion, could not avoid the animal with his Ford Escort car and the accident caused him to drop back to fifth place on the special stage and to third overall.
Sainz was the overnight leader on Sunday and second on Monday, but this incident allowed his Ford team mate Juha Kankunnen of Finland to move up to second behind leading Swede Eriksson in his Subaru.
Eriksson was third on the 19th stage at Te Akau North, run over gravel roads in fine and windy conditions, but consolidated his overall lead.
He now has a total time of three hours 37 minutes 32 seconds, a lead of 24 seconds over four-times champion Kankunnen and 34 over Sainz.
The third leg is the final part of the rally which is scheduled to end later on Tuesday.
